To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have performed a search for dark matter particles using a single germanium detector at the Souda Underground Laboratory and that we have excluded a region in the spin-independent WIMP-nucleus interaction cross section for WIMP masses between 3 and 6  GeV/c2.
we have developed a new technique for detecting low-mass WIMPs, and that our data do not support the existence of such particles in the mass range from 1.6 to 6  Gev/c2.

1) We report a new result using CDMSlite, a calorimetric detector technology, with an ionization energy threshold of 160  eV, and 2) we present a new exclusion limit on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleus scattering cross-section that extends to WIMP particle masses below 6 GeV/c2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of low-mass dark matter, specifically the detection of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) candidates using a germanium detector.
the search for low mass dark matter particles in a 600g germanium detector, which is operated in Soudan Underground Lab (Minnesota, USA).
the development and use of semiconductor-based detectors in the search for dark matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CDMSlite experiment is the most sensitive search for light WIMPs, with a sensitivity that is 10-100 times better than any previous experiment.
this paper is a very nice example of the use of a calorimetric detector to search for WIMP dark matter.
the results of the SuperCDMS Soudan experiment are not in conflict with the null results from other direct detection experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CDMSlite results, in conjunction with existing CDMS results, place the most aggressive bounds on spin-independent WIMP-nucleonic interactions for WIMP masses < 3-6  GeV/cc, depending on the model.
the CDMSlite detector has achieved a new threshold for germanium detectors, which is 10× lower than previous CDMS results.
we have demonstrated the CDMSlite technique and set the lowest energy threshold for a detector with a mass of 0.6  kg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CDMSlite is a powerful technique that can be used for future searches for WIMP-nucleus interactions with masses of 1 GeV/c2 and larger.

the calorimetric ion detection technology is a promising approach to reach sub-keVee energy thresholds and to achieve even better energy resolution, which would allow us to probe a previously unexplored region of parameter space for low-mass WIMPs.
the CDMSlite technique, which was designed to search for low WIMP masses, can be applied broadly to dark matter and rare event searches using Ge detectors.
